content:
AMD has introduced the EPYC Embedded 9006 Series SP7, a family of high-performance x86 SoCs built around the Zen 6 and Zen 6c architectures using a 2nm CPU process. Designed for semiconductor automated test equipment (ATE), networking appliances, firewalls, and enterprise storage controllers, the new embedded processors feature up to 256 cores, 512 threads, and 1GB of L3 cache, with power ratings ranging from 400W to 600W. Compared to the previous-generation EPYC Embedded 9005 Series, the new processors offer 16-channel DDR5 memory with RDIMM and MRDIMM support, up to 96 PCIe Gen 6 lanes, and CXL 3.1 connectivity. They also offer improved security, enterprise-class reliability, and seven-year product availability, making them suitable for long-lifecycle embedded systems.
